problems.title: Constant-delay differential equations in Stan Math
problems.summary: Feature. The C++ functions dde_rk45 and dde_rk45_tol integrate a system with constant delays and propagate sensitivities. Torsten uses the same integrator to resume after dosing events.

commits.title: Add dde_rk45 and dde_rk45_tol: constant-delay DDE solver adapted from RETARD
Make the DDE core a resumable integrator with jumps and jump conditions
Add derivative() to the resumable DDE integrator

fix.why_together: The first commit adds the solver. The next two expose resumable state and the derivative at the current stop, which the Torsten event solver needs.

requires.name: Stan language signatures
requires.why: Required when compiling a Stan model that calls dde_rk45 or dde_rk45_tol. C++ callers use the Math headers directly.

validation.detail: 11 tests passed. Covers sensitivities to initial state, parameters and delays.
4 tests passed. Exercises reverse-mode derivatives across resumable integration.

problems.title: User-supplied Jacobians for ODE, DAE and DDE solvers
problems.summary: Feature. C++ callers can provide derivatives to the solvers and check them against autodiff. Stan Math issue #1061 describes the ODE use case.

commits.title: Prototype ODE solvers taking a user Jacobian; benchmark against nested AD
Jacobian overloads for every ODE solver, adjoint included; tests vs AD
dae/dae_tol overloads taking a residual Jacobian
Check user Jacobians against autodiff: debug flag and Stan-callable checks

fix.why_together: The ODE overload introduces the shared Jacobian adapter. The remaining commits extend it to the other solver families and add derivative checks. Only the DDE overload requires the delay solver.

validation.detail: 4 tests passed, including direct comparisons with autodiff and checks for incorrect Jacobian dimensions.
12 tests passed. Covers the ODE and DAE overloads, the adjoint solver and the Jacobian checking functions.

problems.title: Torsten dosing and delay solvers on Stan Math v5.3.0
problems.summary: Feature. The embedded Torsten Math tree supplies the compartment models and pmx_solve_dde_rk45. The latter combines dosing schedules with the resumable Stan Math integrator.

commits.title: Add Torsten (nsiccha/torsten_math develop) as a subtree at stan/math/torsten
Add Metrum's Torsten hooks: stan/math.hpp include, make files, ARKODE rules
Pull nsiccha/torsten_math develop d884ec18 into the Torsten subtree

fix.why_together: The first subtree import and the build and include hooks expose Torsten in Math. The later subtree pull brings in the dosing DDE solver and the compartment repairs.

requires.name: Embedded Torsten Math revision
requires.why: This revision has exactly the tree stored under stan/math/torsten.

requires.name: Stan language signatures for the PMX DDE solver
requires.why: Use the Torsten-capable compiler when calling pmx_solve_dde_rk45 from Stan.

validation.detail: 12 tests passed. Exercises the integration between Torsten dosing events and the Math delay solver.

problems.title: One-compartment amounts and gradients become NaN when ka equals CL/V
problems.summary: For a depot bolus, the central amount has the finite limit A × ka × t × exp(−ka × t). Dividing by ka − CL/V gives NaN at equality and loses precision nearby.

commits.title: Pull nsiccha/torsten_math develop d884ec18 into the Torsten subtree

fix.why_together: Math imports this code as a squashed Torsten subtree. The single Math commit is the integration point (relative to its first parent). For Torsten Math itself, 65080ee669 contains the complete one-compartment repair and its regression tests.

requires.name: One-compartment propagator and regression
requires.why: This is the independently applicable source patch on Torsten Math develop at bb8266ea6bf2eebdc56e1ba82be230e3b4d70a9a.

validation.detail: 10 tests passed. Includes exact limiting values, gradients and steady state.

problems.title: Two-compartment and effect-compartment solvers lose accuracy or return NaN at coincident rates
problems.summary: Valid rate combinations make the eigenvector formulas singular. One two-compartment effect-model case also fails when ka equals k21, even if the system has distinct eigenvalues. A shared matrix-exponential formula stays finite at these parameter values.

problems.title: The one-compartment effect model returns the wrong steady state at distinct rates
problems.summary: The effect-compartment amount can be zero after dosing into that compartment. With overlapping depot infusions it can disagree with the limit of repeated transient solves even when the rates are distinct.
